title: Why are people drawn to extreme sports? With Eric Brymer, PhD

sentences.en: For most of us, the idea of jumping off a bridge with a parachute or surfing a wave 70 feet high seems to defy comprehension.
sentences.zh: 对于我们大多数人来说，背着降落伞从桥上跳下，或是去冲70英尺高的巨浪，这种想法似乎完全无法理解。

sentences.en: We might regard base jumpers, big wave surfers, free solo rock climbers, and other extreme adventurers with a mixture of confusion, awe, and skepticism,
sentences.zh: 我们可能会用困惑、敬畏和怀疑交织的眼光来看待低空跳伞者、巨浪冲浪者、无绳徒手攀岩者以及其他极限冒险家，

sentences.en: thinking there's no way I could risk my life like that.
sentences.zh: 觉得我绝不可能那样拿自己的生命去冒险。

sentences.en: Psychologists, too, have wondered what drives people to participate in extreme sports, and they're finding that many of our preconceived notions about adventurers are wrong.
sentences.zh: 心理学家也一直在探究究竟是什么驱使人们参与极限运动，而他们发现，我们对冒险者的许多既定看法其实是错误的。

sentences.en: Many extreme adventurers, they argue, are not daredevil risk takers, but instead careful planners who prepare methodically for the adventures they undertake.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，许多极限冒险者并不是好勇斗狠的冒险狂，而是细致的规划者，他们会为自己从事的冒险活动进行有条不紊的准备。

sentences.en: So what does draw people to extreme adventure?
sentences.zh: 那么，究竟是什么吸引人们去进行极限冒险呢？

sentences.en: Do adventurers share any common personality traits?
sentences.zh: 冒险者们有什么共同的性格特征吗？

sentences.en: Do they just have less fear than the rest of us, or do they channel their fear differently?
sentences.zh: 是因为他们比我们其他人更少感到恐惧，还是他们以不同的方式引导了恐惧？

sentences.en: And what role does fear play in how adventurers approach what they do?
sentences.zh: 在冒险者对待他们所做的事情时，恐惧又起到了什么作用？

sentences.en: What lessons can less adventurous people learn from research into extreme adventure?
sentences.zh: 不那么热衷冒险的人，能从对极限冒险的研究中吸取到什么教训？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学话你知》，这是美国心理学协会的旗舰播客，专门探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. Eric Breimer, a psychologist and senior lecturer at Southern Cross University
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是埃里克·布莱默博士，他是一位心理学家，也是澳大利亚南十字星大学的高级讲师，

sentences.en: in Australia, where he studies the human-nature relationship and performance in extreme environments.
sentences.zh: 他在该校研究人与自然的关系以及在极端环境中的表现。

sentences.en: He has interviewed dozens of adventurers for his research studies and is the editor of a recent book, Adventure Psychology, Going Knowingly Into the Unknown.
sentences.zh: 他在研究中采访过数十位冒险者，并且是最近出版的一本书《冒险心理学：知己知彼闯未知》的编辑。

sentences.en: Dr. Breimer, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 布莱默博士，谢谢你今天能来。

sentences.en: Thank you very much for inviting me, Kim.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你的邀请，金。

sentences.en: It's very wonderful to be with you across the pond.
sentences.zh: 隔着大洋能与你相聚，感觉非常美妙。

sentences.en: The big pond.
sentences.zh: 大西洋。

sentences.en: The very big pond.
sentences.zh: 非常非常宽广的大洋。

sentences.en: Well, let's start with a question that I posed in the introduction.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们从我在引言中提出的一个问题开始。

sentences.en: What draws people to participate in activities like base jumping or free solo climbing?
sentences.zh: 是什么吸引人们参与低空跳伞或无绳徒手攀岩等活动？

sentences.en: I mean, you've interviewed a lot of adventurers over the years.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些年来你采访过很多冒险者。

sentences.en: What have they told you about why they do what they do?
sentences.zh: 他们对你倾诉过自己为什么要从事这些活动吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a fascinating question because there's actually two parts to that question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个引人入胜的问题，因为这个问题实际上包含两个部分。

sentences.en: One is, why do people start?
sentences.zh: 一个是人们为什么开始？

sentences.en: And the other one is, why do people continue?
sentences.zh: 另一个是人们为什么坚持？

sentences.en: And they're often very different.
sentences.zh: 这两者往往有很大不同。

sentences.en: So, the traditional notion is the no fear, risk-taking, the kind of death wish notion where people get into these things because they just love to take risks.
sentences.zh: 所以，传统观念认为是没有恐惧、爱冒险、带点求死心态，也就是人们迷上这些事是因为他们纯粹喜欢冒险。

sentences.en: They've got a personality that drives them to look at these kind of activities.
sentences.zh: 他们的个性驱使他们去关注这类活动。

sentences.en: But actually, we find it's very different to that.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我们发现情况大不相同。

sentences.en: The reason people start is as varied as there are people there.
sentences.zh: 人们开始的原因可谓千差万别，正如形形色色的人一样。

sentences.en: I've spoken to some people who said, well, my family is surfers, so I got into surfing.
sentences.zh: 我跟一些人聊过，他们说，哦，我的家人都是冲浪的，所以我才开始冲浪。

sentences.en: But they were the only one that went into big wave surfing.
sentences.zh: 但他们是家里唯一一个去玩巨浪冲浪的人。

sentences.en: I've spoken to people who said, I didn't think I was interested in any of this.
sentences.zh: 我跟一些人聊过，他们说，我本以为自己对这些完全不感兴趣。

sentences.en: I can remember talking to one lady, for sake of example, who called herself a corporate chick.
sentences.zh: 我记得跟一位女士聊过，举个例子，她自称为职场女性。

sentences.en: And she said, only when I went to a corporate motivational talk and I saw this person was describing their life.
sentences.zh: 她说，直到有一次她去听了一场职场励志演讲，听到那个人在描述自己的生活。

sentences.en: And they had images of base jumping because they were a base jumper.
sentences.zh: 对方展示了低空跳伞的照片，因为他是一名低空跳伞者。

sentences.en: They were also medical doctor as well, but they were a base jumper.
sentences.zh: 他同时也是一名医生，但他确实玩低空跳伞。

sentences.en: And she said, something just clicked inside of me.
sentences.zh: 她说，她内心有什么东西突然被触动了。

sentences.en: And I thought, that looks fascinating.
sentences.zh: 然后她想，这看起来太迷人了。

sentences.en: And then she spent six, seven years learning everything she needed to learn in order to start the base jump.
sentences.zh: 接着她花了两三年时间，学习了开始低空跳伞所需的一切知识。

sentences.en: So, there's all sorts of varieties of reasons why people get into it.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们涉足这行的原因可谓五花八门。

sentences.en: And believe it or not, some people get into it because they love the idea of safety and managing sort of, you know, the base jumping association in Australia, for sake of
sentences.zh: 信不信由你，有些人涉足是因为他们喜欢安全的概念，并且喜欢管理那种，比如说，澳大利亚低空跳伞协会的安全官员，

sentences.en: example, has a safety officer.
sentences.zh: 举个例子。

sentences.en: So, there are all sorts of reasons.
sentences.zh: 所以各种原因都有。

sentences.en: And most of those reasons are individual.
sentences.zh: 而且其中大多数原因都是个体的。

sentences.en: They're based on people's particular life at the time, what comes their way.
sentences.zh: 它们基于人们当时特定的生活状态以及迎面而来的经历。

sentences.en: It's not always that there is a kind of framework out there that suggests that their opportunities in their
sentences.zh: 并不总是有某种现成的框架，暗示他们由于某种个性，在特定环境中拥有某种机遇，

sentences.en: particular environment, because they have a personality, they just go and do it.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就会直接去做了。

sentences.en: But we also find that's not quite true either.
sentences.zh: 但我们也发现事实并非完全如此。

sentences.en: I've spoken to people who, you know, were born and bred and brought up in a city.
sentences.zh: 我跟一些人聊过，你知道的，他们是在城市里土生土长的人。

sentences.en: But one particular person said, ever since he can remember, he was just really fascinated by stories of the mountains.
sentences.zh: 但其中一个人说，自从他记事起，他就对高山的故事非常着迷。

sentences.en: And he used to read mountain stories, mountaineering stories, all those sort of things.
sentences.zh: 他经常阅读高山故事、登山故事以及诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: Soon he was old enough, he moved to the mountain areas and started to learn how to climb and mountaineer and all those sort of things, when he could do that on his own.
sentences.zh: 等他到了合适的年龄，他就搬到了山区，开始学习如何攀岩、登山以及所有这些在他能独自完成时可以做的事情。

sentences.en: I've spoken to people who lived in the middle of Australia that just had this kind of connection or fascination with the surf.
sentences.zh: 我跟住在澳大利亚中部的人聊过，他们对冲浪有着某种天然的联系或迷恋。

sentences.en: As soon as they were old enough, as soon as they could, they moved to the coast to start developing skills and activities within surfing.
sentences.zh: 只要年龄允许，只要条件允许，他们就会搬到海边，开始培养冲浪的技能和活动。

sentences.en: So, why people get into it is, you know, it's a personal thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们为什么会入行，你知道的，这是一件很个人的事。

sentences.en: And I'll be honest, there are actually some people get into it because they see these videos on YouTube, they hear this heavy rock music, and they think,
sentences.zh: 说实话，确实有些人入行是因为他们在优酷上看到了这些视频，听到强烈的摇滚乐，然后觉得，

sentences.en: this is exciting and thrilling.
sentences.zh: 这太刺激、太惊险了。

sentences.en: I'll get into that and I'll give that a go.
sentences.zh: 我要去玩这个，我要去尝试一下。

sentences.en: But often what happens with those people is either they very quickly realize it's not quite as simple as they thought
sentences.zh: 但这些人的结局往往是，要么他们很快发现事情并没有想象的那么简单，

sentences.en: it actually takes a lot of commitment and hard work and training, etc.
sentences.zh: 这实际上需要大量的承诺、辛苦的训练等等，

sentences.en: to do this well.
sentences.zh: 才能把这件事做好。

sentences.en: Or if they're lucky, they have an accident, which means they can't do it anymore.
sentences.zh: 或者如果他们运气好，出了次事故，这意味着他们再也玩不了了。

sentences.en: But often it's they die.
sentences.zh: 但通常的结果是他们丧命。

sentences.en: And then they just can't continue.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就再也无法继续下去了。

sentences.en: So, they drop out pretty quickly.
sentences.zh: 所以他们很快就会退圈。

sentences.en: So, that brings us on to the next element is why people continue.
sentences.zh: 这就把我们带到了下一个要素，即人们为什么会坚持下去。

sentences.en: And that's the really fascinating question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个真正引人入胜的问题。

sentences.en: Because what we're definitely finding is the idea of the traditional idea of no fear,
sentences.zh: 因为我们非常确切地发现，传统的“无所畏惧”、

sentences.en: having a death wish, having a risk taking or type of personality doesn't fit the extreme sports athlete.
sentences.zh: “有求死心态”、“喜欢冒险”或某种特定个性的观点，并不符合极限运动健儿的特征。

sentences.en: In fact, we find they're very careful.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们发现他们非常谨慎。

sentences.en: We find that in fact, they have an in-depth knowledge of the environment that they are participating in.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，他们对所参与的环境有着深入的了解。

sentences.en: We find that actually, it takes years and they do some really intense training to get to the skills.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，这实际上需要数年的时间，而且他们会进行非常密集的训练来掌握这些技能。

sentences.en: One base jumper, for sake of example, before they started proximity flying.
sentences.zh: 比如有一个低空跳伞者，在他开始翼装飞行之前。

sentences.en: And for those who don't know, proximity flying is when you jump off a cliff, but you have a wingsuit and then you fly along the cliff as far as you can and travel for a distance
sentences.zh: 对于那些不了解的人来说，翼装飞行就是你从悬崖上跳下，穿着一件翼装，然后沿着悬崖尽可能远地飞行，滑行一段距离，

sentences.en: before you pull your parachute.
sentences.zh: 然后再打开降落伞。

sentences.en: But before he transitioned from base jumping to wingsuit, he spent years researching across the world every single potential accident in order to figure out
sentences.zh: 但在他从低空跳伞过渡到翼装飞行之前，他花了数年时间研究全球发生的每一个潜在事故，以便找出

sentences.en: whether there were patterns.
sentences.zh: 其中是否存在规律。

sentences.en: And then he did find patterns.
sentences.zh: 后来他确实找到了规律。

sentences.en: And he decided, well, okay, these are the patterns where things go wrong.
sentences.zh: 于是他决定，好吧，这些就是出问题时的规律。

sentences.en: I'm going to avoid those.
sentences.zh: 我要避开这些情况。

sentences.en: And this is not an unusual kind of activity at all.
sentences.zh: 这绝对不是什么罕见的操作。

sentences.en: So, people really get a profound, not only the environment, but profound knowledge of the activity they're doing.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们不仅对环境，而且对自己正在从事的活动有着深刻的认识。

sentences.en: The other thing that happens as well, and people start at different levels here, is that because extreme sports athletes are basically on their own, if
sentences.zh: 还有一件事，虽然人们在这里的起点各不相同，那就是因为极限运动健儿基本都是孤身一人，如果在极限运动过程中

sentences.en: something goes wrong in the middle of an extreme sport activity, nobody can help you out.
sentences.zh: 出了问题，没有人能帮得了你。

sentences.en: The only person that's there for you is yourself.
sentences.zh: 唯一能在那里帮助你的人只有你自己。

sentences.en: So, you have to have a really profound, deep knowledge of your capacities, of what you're capable of and how you're feeling and all those sort of things.
sentences.zh: 因此，你必须对自己的能力、自己能胜任什么、你的感觉如何以及所有这些事情有着非常深刻、透彻的了解。

sentences.en: Because if you're not feeling right, if things aren't quite right, or you have the sense that
sentences.zh: 因为如果你感觉不对劲，如果情况有些不对，或者你隐隐觉得

sentences.en: something is not right, it might just be the winds in the wrong direction, or something isn't sort of feeling well.
sentences.zh: 有什么不对劲，可能只是风向不对，或者身体感觉不太舒服。

sentences.en: You have to have the capacity to say, well, actually, you know what, I'm going to walk away.
sentences.zh: 你必须有勇气说，好吧，你知道吗，我要走开。

sentences.en: I'll come back again another day, because today doesn't feel good.
sentences.zh: 我改天再来，因为今天感觉不对。

sentences.en: And that happens more than you realize within an extreme sport context as well.
sentences.zh: 在极限运动的语境中，这种情况发生的频率比你想象的还要多。

sentences.en: And the people that I interviewed weren't in the typical age that we think about extreme athletes as well.
sentences.zh: 而且我采访过的人也并非我们想象中极限运动员的典型年龄。

sentences.en: I mean, they weren't the sort of older teenagers, younger 20s.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们不是那种十几岁或二十出头的年轻人。

sentences.en: The youngest person was just over 30, and the oldest person was in their
sentences.zh: 最年轻的刚过30岁，而最年长的人则在
70多岁。

sentences.en: And they were still participating in their particular chosen extreme sport, the ones that they had chosen.
sentences.zh: 他们依然在参与他们各自选择的极限运动。

sentences.en: The last element of this is because of that requirement of the in-depth knowledge of the environment, we often find that extreme athletes, they're not people that go out and
sentences.zh: 这其中的最后一个要素是，正因为需要对环境有深入的了解，我们经常发现极限运动员并不是那种跑出去、

sentences.en: how can I demonstrate my risk-taking activity here today?
sentences.zh: “我今天要怎么在这里展示我爱冒险的举动呢？”的人。

sentences.en: Oh, look, I'll just grab a mountain bike and try and do this, or I'll grab this.
sentences.zh: “哦，看呐，我随便抓辆山地自行车来试着玩一下，或者抓起这个试试。”

sentences.en: They're very focused in the activity, because they learn so much about it.
sentences.zh: 他们对活动非常专注，因为他们对它了解得太多了。

sentences.en: It's very rare to find that people do more than one activity.
sentences.zh: 极少有人会同时从事多项活动。

sentences.en: Or if they do, it's because they need the skills to, say, climb a mountain in order to jump off if they're a base jumper.
sentences.zh: 或者如果有的话，那也是因为他们需要某些技能，比如爬山，以便作为低空跳伞者从山顶跳下。

sentences.en: So, they need a certain element of skills to get to the particular place.
sentences.zh: 所以他们需要掌握特定的技能来去往特定的地方。

sentences.en: But really, their main activity is base jumping.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，他们的主要活动还是低空跳伞。

sentences.en: So, in a summary, basically, there's two elements of motivations, why people get into it, and why people continue.
sentences.zh: 总而言之，基本上有两个动机要素：人们为什么入行，以及人们为什么坚持。

sentences.en: And they're very different.
sentences.zh: 这两者大不相同。

sentences.en: What you're describing is a really interesting level of meticulousness.
sentences.zh: 你所描述的是一种非常引人注目的细致入微的程度。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering whether these people are as meticulous about everything else in their lives?
sentences.zh: 我在想，这些人对他们生活中的其他事情也同样如此一丝不苟吗？

sentences.en: That's a very good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: They are definitely – well, there's two elements to that one as well, unfortunately.
sentences.zh: 他们确实是——不过不幸的是，这里面也有两个要素。

sentences.en: One is that doing the adventure and the extreme sport does change your attitude in everyday life as well.
sentences.zh: 一个是进行冒险和极限运动确实也会改变你在日常生活中的态度。

sentences.en: And it changes the way you interact with others, the way you experience your relationship with the natural world.
sentences.zh: 它改变了你与他人互动的方式，改变了你体验与自然世界关系的方式。

sentences.en: It changes the way you experience everyday activities.
sentences.zh: 它改变了你体验日常活动的方式。

sentences.en: For such an example, you may still feel a little bit nervous public speaking if you're not used to it.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，如果你不习惯公开演讲，你可能仍然会感到有些紧张。

sentences.en: But people often report utilizing their extreme sports skills to work with that and say, well, you know, in the end, I have these feelings in other places.
sentences.zh: 但人们经常报告说，他们会利用自己的极限运动技能来应对这种情况，并会想，好吧，总之我在其他地方也有过这种感觉。

sentences.en: So, I should be able to do this as well.
sentences.zh: 所以我也应该能应付这个。

sentences.en: If meticulousness means over, you know, over cautious, over specific, over, you know, a perfectionist, if you like, then I would say no,
sentences.zh: 如果一丝不苟意味着过度谨慎、过度具体、过度执着于完美主义，如果你愿意这么说的话，那我可以说不是，

sentences.en: because actually life becomes a lot more enjoyable, a lot more fun, a lot more sort of, you know, you're less concerned about some of the minor things that we may, who, you know,
sentences.zh: 因为实际上生活变得更有乐趣、更有趣、更……你知道的，你不再那么在意那些我们这些

sentences.en: not extreme sport athletes consider to be very important.
sentences.zh: 非极限运动爱好者认为非常重要的小事。

sentences.en: I remember, you know, extreme athletes talking about how they interact with others.
sentences.zh: 我记得极限运动员谈论过他们如何与他人互动。

sentences.en: And, you know, before I was an adventurer, I used to get really concerned when people were really cross with me or really disappointed where I used to work.
sentences.zh: 而且，在我成为冒险者之前，当我在工作的地方遇到别人对我很生气或非常失望时，我会感到非常焦虑。

sentences.en: Now, it doesn't bother me.
sentences.zh: 现在，这根本困扰不到我。

sentences.en: I just think, well, okay, that's, you know, they're having a bad day.
sentences.zh: 我只会想，好吧，那是因为，你知道的，他们今天过得不顺。

sentences.en: That's their problem, not mine.
sentences.zh: 那是他们的问题，不是我的。

sentences.en: I remember speaking to a doctor.
sentences.zh: 我记得曾与一位医生交谈过。

sentences.en: And that was because research up to the time I started had not made that clear.

sentences.en: So they would use the notion of kayaking, or they would use the notion of mountaineering.

sentences.en: But actually, when you dig very closely into it, there's a big difference between kayaking on flat water and kayaking in grade six.

sentences.en: Flat water, you get a bit wet, and maybe, you know, you get a bit cold, depending where you are.

sentences.en: If you come out of your boat, if things go wrong, grade six, if things go wrong, then you are, the chances are you will die.
sentences.zh: 如果你从船里翻出来，要是出了岔子，在六级激流中，一旦出了岔子，你十有八九会丧命。

sentences.en: So one of the things that I did was to say, well, okay, exactly the question you asked me, what makes an extreme sport an extreme sport?
sentences.zh: 所以，我当时做的事情之一就是说，好吧，正如你刚才问我的那样，究竟是什么让极限运动成为极限运动？

sentences.en: And so the first thing we looked at is, if you take this as a continuum, the first thing is that they're interacting in the natural world.
sentences.zh: 我们首先探讨的是，如果把这看作一个连续体，首要的一点是它们是在自然界中进行的。

sentences.en: So the activity takes place in the natural world.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，这项活动发生在自然环境中。

sentences.en: So that means the environment is not so constrained as a basketball environment or a cricket environment or something.
sentences.zh: 这意味着其环境不像篮球场或板球场那样受到诸多限制。

sentences.en: So the environment is free.
sentences.zh: 因此，环境是自由的。

sentences.en: There isn't sort of a, there aren't lines and regulations to say this is in and that is out, which is really important because that's part of the decision
sentences.zh: 这里没有界线和规则来划分界内或界外，这一点真的非常重要，因为它是决策过程的一部分

sentences.en: making process, a problem solving process.
sentences.zh: 也是解决问题过程的一部分。

sentences.en: The second one is potential outcomes or the most likely outcome if things go wrong is that you're dead.
sentences.zh: 第二点是潜在结果，或者说如果出了问题最可能的结果就是死亡。

sentences.en: You're lucky if you get seriously injured and people have been lucky, but the most likely outcome if things go wrong and you haven't been able
sentences.zh: 如果你只是受重伤就算你走运了，以前确实有人挺走运的，但如果出了问题而你又没能

sentences.en: to resolve it quickly is that you die.
sentences.zh: 迅速化解危机，最可能的结果就是丧命。

sentences.en: And that's unlikely to happen in basketball.
sentences.zh: 这在篮球运动中是几乎不会发生的。

sentences.en: I remember one participant saying, you know, they were describing the difference between something like,
sentences.zh: 我记得有个参与者说过，你知道，他们当时在描述某种运动与……之间的区别

sentences.en: actually they use basketball because they were from the US and they're a particular extreme sport.
sentences.zh: 实际上他们举了篮球的例子，因为他们来自美国，并且从事某种特定的极限运动。

sentences.en: And they said, you imagine every time you've missed a goal in basketball, somebody shot you in the head.
sentences.zh: 他们说，试想一下，你在篮球比赛中每投丢一个球，就有人朝你的头部开枪。

sentences.en: That's the difference between extreme sports and basketball.
sentences.zh: 这就是极限运动与篮球的区别。

sentences.en: So basketball can be extreme, but perhaps we don't want to play that game because we'd end up with a lot of accidents and a lot of dead basketball players.
sentences.zh: 所以篮球也可以很极限，但也许我们不想玩那种游戏，因为那样最终会产生大量事故和许多丧命的篮球运动员。

sentences.en: The last element, which is really, really important is that they're independent activities in the sense that they are self-directed.
sentences.zh: 最后一个要素，也是非常非常重要的一个，就是它们是独立的活动，在这个意义上它们是自主导向的。

sentences.en: You can't undertake an extreme sport as what we understand as a teamwork activity, or it's very difficult to do that because in the
sentences.zh: 你无法将极限运动作为我们通常理解的团队协作活动来进行，或者说很难做到这一点，因为归根结底

sentences.en: end, most extreme sports are, whilst you might have colleagues with you and once you make the
sentences.zh: 大多数极限运动——尽管你身边可能有同伴，一旦你在低空跳伞中纵身一跃

sentences.en: jump in a base jump or once you get on the wave in a big wave surf, or once you decide to go over that waterfall, you are on your own.
sentences.zh: 或者在冲大浪时冲上浪头，又或者你决定冲下那个瀑布，你就只能靠自己了。

sentences.en: Some people tend to think of those who participate in these kinds of sports as adrenaline junkies.
sentences.zh: 有些人往往认为参与这类运动的人是肾上腺素瘾君子。

sentences.en: In other words, they have something that's akin to an addiction.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他们患有某种类似瘾症的东西。

sentences.en: Is that notion accurate?
sentences.zh: 这种看法准确吗？

sentences.en: The notion of addiction is really interesting.
sentences.zh: 瘾症这个概念真的很有意思。

sentences.en: I won't get down that pathway.
sentences.zh: 我不会深入探讨这个方向。

sentences.en: I'm sure that's for another day.
sentences.zh: 我确信那是改天再聊的话题。

sentences.en: But if we take the addiction as something that is harmful to you, something that
sentences.zh: 但如果我们把瘾症理解为对你有害的事物，某种

sentences.en: actually is bad for you, ends up damaging in some way, then most definitely not, unless things go wrong, of course.
sentences.zh: 确实对你不好的东西、最终会以某种方式造成损害的事物，那么绝对不是，当然，除非出了意外。

sentences.en: Because actually, what we find is for most participants, the reason they continue is because they get something so powerfully transformational and beneficial from it that
sentences.zh: 因为实际上我们发现，对于大多数参与者而言，他们坚持下去的原因是他们从中获得了如此强大、具有变革意义且有益的体验，以至于

sentences.en: is akin to flourishing, thriving, is akin to all those kind of mystical things that people search for.
sentences.zh: 这类似于繁荣、蓬勃发展，类似于人们所追求的那些神秘体验。

sentences.en: That's why they can keep going, because it's that sort of element of it.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们能够坚持下去的原因，因为正是这种特质。

sentences.en: If we consider it in terms of something about it that drives you to continue doing it, then again, it's not a negative concept that drives you to continue doing it.
sentences.zh: 如果我们从某种驱使你继续从事它的驱动力来看，它同样不是一个促使你继续的消极概念。

sentences.en: It's that more positive element, the sort of the more flourishing, thriving, high levels of well-being, the feelings of freedom,
sentences.zh: 而是那种更积极的要素，那种更具繁荣感、蓬勃发展感、高度幸福感以及自由感、

sentences.en: flying, the kind of ineffable, all those sort of things that provides the opportunity to keep going.
sentences.zh: 飞翔感的体验，正是所有这些难以言表的事物提供了让人不断前行的动力。

sentences.en: The other element which really indicates that it's not akin to an addiction is that we find that extreme athletes are really keen to give back.
sentences.zh: 另一个真正表明它不等同于瘾症的因素是，我们发现极限运动员非常热衷于回馈社会。

sentences.en: They're really keen to work for the environment that they participate in.
sentences.zh: 他们非常热衷于保护他们所参与其中的环境。

sentences.en: So we have extreme athletes, world-renowned extreme athletes who travel the world, you know, defending and trying to talk about the oceans and how we should be protecting them
sentences.zh: 所以我们看到极限运动员，世界知名的极限运动员环游世界，你知道的，为海洋辩护，并试图谈论海洋以及我们应该如何保护它们

sentences.en: and looking after them.
sentences.zh: 和照料它们。

sentences.en: Or we have extreme skiers going around the world looking at, you know, trying to get people to think more carefully about climate change because of what's happening to the
sentences.zh: 或者我们看到极限滑雪者环游世界，你知道的，试图让人们更加认真地思考气候变化问题，因为山地环境

sentences.en: environment in the mountains.
sentences.zh: 正在发生变化。

sentences.en: So actually, what we get is a really positive outcome from it.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，我们从中获得了非常积极的结果。

sentences.en: It's, I mean, if we say that mindfulness-based work, or if we say that those sort of things are
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果我们说基于正念的工作，或者说如果我们将这类事物归为

sentences.en: addictive, then because they're really positive and powerful and people want to keep doing them, then perhaps there's some similarity between addiction.
sentences.zh: 成瘾性的，那么因为它们真的很积极、很有力量，而且人们想要一直做下去，所以或许它与成瘾有某些相似之处。

sentences.en: But where we are at the moment, the indications are definitely not.
sentences.zh: 但就目前的情况来看，种种迹象表明绝对不是。

sentences.en: Are there parallels between people who pursue extreme sports and people who pursue other types
sentences.zh: 追求极限运动的人与追求其他类型极限体验的人之间，是否存在相似之处

sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个非常有趣的问题。

sentences.zh: 如果有哪位间谍朋友想要参与研究项目，请联系我。

sentences.en: But if we look at a comparison between people who do extreme sports and people who
sentences.zh: 但如果我们把极限运动参与者和那些从事其他活动的人进行比较

sentences.en: do those other activities, there are some differences in the sense that an extreme sport is generally speaking a leisure-based activity.
sentences.zh: 会发现存在一些差异，因为极限运动广义上讲是一项基于休闲的活动。

sentences.en: It's something that people do.
sentences.zh: 这是人们会去做的事情。

sentences.en: If you're lucky, you get sponsored to do these sort of things.
sentences.zh: 如果你够幸运，你会得到赞助来做这些事情。

sentences.en: But for most people, it's something they do in their own time.
sentences.zh: 但对大多数人来说，这是他们在自己时间里做的事情。

sentences.en: So they aren't linked.

sentences.en: They aren't combined.

sentences.en: There's no necessity to do it.

sentences.en: There isn't any of those outside forces that come into it that indicate that this is something that they almost need to do because
sentences.zh: 这里面没有任何外部力量促使他们觉得这几乎是他们必须去做的事情，因为

sentences.en: So that separates the two already.

sentences.zh: 第二个要素是，不久前曾有过一些研究，试图用心理动力学理论来解释极限潜水。

sentences.zh: 我认为他们在解释为什么有些人会进行极限潜水方面做得很好。

sentences.zh: 但实际上，它并没有很好地解释为什么所有人都会这样做。

sentences.en: And there are definitely people who get involved who might have particular issues outside and they want to kind of do these things.

sentences.en: But that's a very small percentage of people that get involved.
sentences.zh: 但这只是参与其中的一小部分人。

sentences.en: So I think the short answer to that is no.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为对此简短的回答是“不”。

sentences.en: And for all sorts of different reasons.
sentences.zh: 原因形形色色。

sentences.en: different kind of personality to become a Navy SEAL or to become a spy or whatever it might be.
sentences.zh: 你必须具备一种不同的性格。

sentences.en: And I'd say I'm not an expert in those areas at all.
sentences.zh: 我要说的是，我根本不是这些领域的专家。

sentences.en: So I'm hoping I'm not commenting in a way that's sort of derogatory to them.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望我的评论不会以某种贬低他们的方式展开。

sentences.en: It's probably easier to say that if something goes wrong, you may be likely because to be a personality of type, but not to

sentences.en: participate, not to do things well, not to explore what an extreme sport can offer.
sentences.zh: 所以有各种迹象表明，实际上参与极限运动与某些其他危险活动

sentences.en: So there's all sorts of indications that actually participating in extreme sport is not similar to some other
sentences.zh: 或者需要特定行为方式的活动并不相似。

sentences.en: activities where things might be dangerous or they might be, you know, require a particular way of behaving.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，也有一些非常相似的地方，比如当你做某事时那种油然而生的平静感，这在极限运动中绝对显而易见。

sentences.en: Having said that, there are also things that could be very similar, such as the sense of calm when you're doing something that definitely comes across in extreme sports.

sentences.en: And I can imagine as a spy and as a Navy SEAL, et cetera, you'd need to have a sense of calm in really dangerous situations.

sentences.en: And extreme sports athletes have that sense of calm.

sentences.en: But once I leap, once I make the decision to go, in many ways, I have to just let go.
sentences.zh: 我必须臣服于当下，全神贯注地融入那个当下，以便能够与那种环境进行如此高效的互动

sentences.en: I have to surrender to the moment and be so much so present in that moment that I can interact with that environment so effectively
sentences.zh: 以至于如果真的出了岔子，举个例子，我能够解决问题，或者我能够享受其中，能够与环境充分交融从而与之嬉戏。

sentences.en: that if things do go wrong, for sake of example, I can fix them or I can enjoy, I can be with the environment enough that I can play with it.
sentences.zh: 我能与它共舞。

sentences.en: I can be in a dance with it.
sentences.zh: 我能与那个环境协同运作。

sentences.en: I can be working with that environment.
sentences.zh: 我可以想象，如果你是一名间谍或海豹突击队员，情况可能也是如此。

sentences.en: And I could imagine that's probably very similar if you're a spy or if you're a Navy SEAL as well.
sentences.zh: 你可以规划你所能规划的，但归根结底，环境在任何发生的事情中也扮演着一定角色。

sentences.en: You plan what you can, but in the end, the environment also has a role in that, in whatever happens.
sentences.zh: 因此，你必须完全顺应环境中的信息，以便在此时此地做出决策。

sentences.en: And therefore, you have to be totally attuned to the information in that environment to make decisions in the here and now.
sentences.zh: 我认为这与极限运动运动员非常相似。

sentences.en: And that is very similar, I think, to an extreme sports athlete.
sentences.zh: 让我们花一分钟来谈谈恐惧。

sentences.en: Let's talk for a minute about fear.
sentences.zh: 许多人可能会认为这些探险家是无所畏惧的，但你却认为他们其实心怀强烈的恐惧。

sentences.en: A lot of people might assume that these adventurers are fearless, but you argue that they actually have a lot of fear.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们需要恐惧才能完成他们所做的事情。

sentences.en: And in fact, they need to have fear in order to do what they do.
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下吗？

sentences.en: Can you explain that?
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 我们对其中的微妙之处还不是十分确定，但总的来说，“毫无恐惧”这种想法——认为只有这样才能完成任务——在极限运动的语境下是行不通的。

sentences.en: We're not quite sure of the nuances yet, but broadly, the idea of having no fear, that's the only way you can do that, doesn't work in extreme sport context.
sentences.zh: 行不通的原因是，如果你毫无恐惧，就说明你没有认真对待自己正在做的事情。

sentences.en: The reason it doesn't work is because if you have no fear, you're not taking what you're doing seriously.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有认真对待自己做的事，就意味着你不会去关注环境中那些真正微妙的信息，不会关注自身等等。

sentences.en: And if you don't take what you're doing seriously, it means you're not going to pay attention to the real sort of fine information in their environment, to yourself, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 那样的话，事情就很可能会出错。

sentences.en: And it's likely that things will go wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们实际发现的是，极限运动运动员非常严肃地看待恐惧。

sentences.en: So, what we actually find is that extreme sports athletes take fear seriously.
sentences.zh: 事实上，恐惧对他们来说非常重要，因为它发出了警报：请注意。

sentences.en: And in fact, fear is really important to them in the sense that it's saying, pay attention.
sentences.zh: 当你产生这种恐惧感时，意味着你更加严肃地对待自己正在做的事。

sentences.en: When you have that sense of fear, it means you take what you're doing more seriously.
sentences.zh: 你会关注环境中的所有线索和信息。

sentences.en: You pay attention to all the cues and the information in the environment.
sentences.zh: 你会关注自己的身体感受。

sentences.en: You pay attention to how you're feeling.
sentences.zh: 你会确保自己已经做好了所有适当的准备工作等等。

sentences.en: You really make sure that you've done all the preparation, et cetera, properly.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你愿意的话，恐惧就是一种注意力的触发器，或者是一个促进因素，提醒你需要认真对待此事。

sentences.en: So, fear, if you like, is a trigger to pay attention or a facilitator to sort of suggest that you need to take this seriously.
sentences.zh: 如果你不认真对待，这件事就可能会导致灾难性的后果。

sentences.en: This is something, if you don't take seriously, can go disastrously wrong.
sentences.zh: 因此我们发现，极限运动运动员所做的反而是学会利用恐惧作为一种信号，提醒自己：等一下，我这种感觉是在暗示着什么。

sentences.en: So, we find instead that what extreme sports athletes are doing is learning to utilize fear as a way of saying, hang on a minute, this feeling I'm getting is suggesting something.
sentences.zh: 到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: What is it that's going on?
sentences.zh: 举个例子，一个处于专注状态中的极限滑雪者突然产生了一种感觉。

sentences.en: And it might be, for sake of an example, an extreme skier who is in that sort of sense of being present suddenly gets a sensation.
sentences.zh: 他们能感受到恐惧的降临，起初他们不知道为什么，但也许是感知系统捕捉到了一点噪音、某种感觉、气味

sentences.en: They can feel the sensation of fear and they don't know why to begin with, but maybe the perceptual systems have picked up a bit of a noise or a feeling or a smell
sentences.zh: 或者一种触觉上的寒意，接着他们就会关注环境并心想：啊，可能会有雪崩。

sentences.en: or a cool, a haptic kind of, and then they can pay attention to the environment and think, ah, there could be an avalanche.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就知道自己该做些什么了。

sentences.en: And then they know what they need to do.
sentences.zh: 或者低空跳伞运动员也可能会做类似的事情。

sentences.en: Or a base jumper might do something similar.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会感受一下气流并心想：等一下，我以为风向应该是这样的，但这有点不对劲。

sentences.en: They might feel the air and think, hang on a minute, I thought it was supposed to be doing this, but this isn't quite right.
sentences.zh: 这里有什么事情不对劲。

sentences.en: Something is not happening here.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会意识到并加以关注：实际上，空气流动的方向或风向与我原先想象的并不一样。

sentences.en: And they might realize and they can pay attention, actually, the air is going a different direction or the wind is going a different direction than I thought it was going.
sentences.zh: 所以，所有这些由恐惧所激发的细微线索都真的非常非常重要。

sentences.en: So, all those little cues that are facilitated by fear are really, really important.
sentences.zh: 它在提醒：注意。

sentences.en: It says, pay attention.
sentences.zh: 这很严肃。

sentences.en: This is serious.
sentences.zh: 我们目前还不太确定的是，这种感觉究竟是怎样的机制，是先产生恐惧感——显然，捕捉到环境中的某些信息是其中一个环节。

sentences.en: What we're not quite sure yet is whether the sensation, what happens first, the sensation of fear, obviously, there's an element of picking up something in the environment.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一种传入身体的感觉，提示你要注意。

sentences.en: And that might be a sensation that comes into the body that says, pay attention.
sentences.zh: 但我们并不完全清楚这究竟是直接传达“注意”的具体信息，还是先给你一种体感，然后你才去寻找那些提示你需要注意的信息。

sentences.en: But we don't quite know whether it's actual information that says, pay attention, or whether it's giving you the kind of a bit of a
sentences.zh: 所以，这个微小的细节虽未完全定论，但它确实是一个非常关键的要素。

sentences.en: sensation that you then have to look out for information that says, pay attention.
sentences.zh: 我在想，近年来对极限运动或探险运动的兴趣是否有所增加，还是说这只是我们的错觉，因为我们在媒体和网络上看到了

sentences.en: So, that little nuance is not quite there, but it's actually a really important element.
sentences.zh: 大量关于这类事情的报道？

sentences.en: I'm wondering if interest in extreme or adventure sports has increased in recent years, or does it just seem that way because we're seeing a lot more coverage of these sorts of
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: things in the media and online?
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们确实看到了更多报道，这绝对是件好事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，参与人数确实也增加了。

sentences.en: I think we are seeing more, which is definitely good.
sentences.zh: 英国曾做过一份报告——美国也有一份，英国有一份，中国也有一份。

sentences.en: But actually, it has increased as well.
sentences.zh: 在英国，探险运动是增长最快的运动。

sentences.en: A report done in the UK, well, there's one done in America, there's one in the UK, and there's one done in China too.
sentences.zh: 因此，55%参与体育锻炼和运动的人都在进行某种探险活动。

sentences.en: In the UK, adventure sports are the fastest growing sport.
sentences.zh: 这大概是四五年前的数据了。

sentences.en: So, 55% of people involved in physical activity and sport are doing something adventurous.
sentences.zh: 美国也做过类似的调查，他们发现全美对探险以及更极端探险的热情出现了巨大的增长。

sentences.en: This was maybe four or five years ago.
sentences.zh: 这大概是四五年前的数据了。

sentences.en: The US has done something similar, and they see massive rises in an adventure and more extreme adventures across the US.
sentences.zh: 美国也做过类似的调查，他们发现全美对探险以及更极端探险的热情出现了巨大的增长。

sentences.en: China, in a slightly lower level, has seen enormous increases in people doing things like mountaineering and hill walking and things like that.
sentences.zh: 在中国，在稍低的层面上，我们可以看到参与登山、远足等活动的人数大幅增加。

sentences.en: Millions of people doing it now.
sentences.zh: 现在有数百万人参与其中。

sentences.en: And India, the same.
sentences.zh: 印度也是如此。

sentences.en: Partially, the change is due to the tourism aspect of extreme sports, the more adventure tourism element of it, where people can come and have these experiences.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是极限运动带来的旅游业转变，即更多的探险旅游元素，人们可以来这里体验。

sentences.en: They may not have the skills and expertise to do it themselves, but they can do something in a context that means there is somebody who is an expert in that area who can manage and
sentences.zh: 他们可能没有亲自完成这些活动的技能和专业知识，但他们可以在某个环境中进行，这意味着该领域会有专家来管理和

sentences.en: rafting, for sake of example, or group bushwalking activities, or maybe you go on a three or four day camp or something like that.
sentences.zh: 比如漂流，或者集体远足活动，或者你可能会去参加一个三四天的露营之类的。

sentences.en: So, those kind of activities are happening.
sentences.zh: 所以，这类活动正在发生。

sentences.en: So, there's definitely a massive increase across the world, as I say, partially driven by tourism, but also driven by recreational activities, too.
sentences.zh: 因此，正如我所说，世界各地绝对出现了大幅增长，部分是由旅游业推动的，但也是由休闲活动推动的。

sentences.en: People choosing to do it.
sentences.zh: 人们选择这样做。

sentences.en: And that might also be why there are so many people, even though part of it is to do with the technology, but we see so much more because more
sentences.zh: 这也可能是为什么有这么多人——尽管部分原因与技术有关——但我们看到得更多，是因为更多

sentences.en: people are interested in looking at them and watching them and imagining themselves in those
sentences.zh: 的人有兴趣观看、观赏，并想象自己置身于那些

sentences.en: contexts or dreaming of the next time they could go away and do that kayak trip or whatever it might be.
sentences.zh: 情境中，或者梦想着下一次他们可以去进行那次皮划艇之旅，无论那是什么。

sentences.en: And I think that's kind of a reciprocal thing.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种相互促进的事情。

sentences.en: The more people do it, the more people are interested, the more they want to see more, the more it goes on like this.
sentences.zh: 越多的人参与，越多的人感兴趣，他们就越想看到更多，事情就会这样不断发展下去。

sentences.en: It's a bit of a spiral, an upward spiral, luckily.
sentences.zh: 这有点像个螺旋，幸运的是，这是一个上升的螺旋。

sentences.en: It does have a downside.
sentences.zh: 它确实有不好的一面。

sentences.en: All this technology has a downside.
sentences.zh: 所有这些技术都有不好的一面。

sentences.en: And the downside, for sake of example, is you could watch something that is undertaken by an extreme
sentences.zh: 举个例子，不好的一面是，你可能会观看由极限

sentences.en: sports expert, and you don't realize that they spent 10 or 15 years developing the skills to be able to do what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 运动专家进行的活动，而你却没有意识到他们花了两三年甚至十几年才培养出能够做到这一点的技能。

sentences.en: And you think, oh, that looks interesting and exciting.
sentences.zh: 然后你会想，哦，这看起来既有趣又刺激。

sentences.en: I can't do that myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己也行。

sentences.en: To a certain extent, you can't do the very extreme level yourself because you don't have the skills and expertise and you wouldn't know what to buy and all those sort of things.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，你无法亲自完成极端的水平，因为你没有技能和专业知识，你也不知道该买什么等等。

sentences.en: But it does open up the potential for people doing things that perhaps they don't have the skills and expertise to do.
sentences.zh: 但它确实为人们打开了从事那些他们可能没有技能和专业知识去做的活动的潜力。

sentences.en: Technology has driven that to an extent.
sentences.zh: 技术在某种程度上推动了这一点。

sentences.en: For sake of example, in my activity, whitewater kayaking, the one I prefer to do, when I started, all boats were fiberglass.
sentences.zh: 举个我自己的活动的例子，白水皮划艇，这是我最喜欢的，我刚开始的时候，所有的船都是玻璃纤维的。

sentences.en: So if you bumped in a rock, you'd have a great big hole and you'd be swimming.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你撞到岩石，就会有一个大洞，然后你就得在水里游了。

sentences.en: Once boats became plastic, you could bump in a rock and it's a bit like a pinball machine.
sentences.zh: 一旦船变成了塑料的，你撞到岩石时就有点像弹珠机。

sentences.en: You bump on one rock and bump on another rock and you bump on another rock and eventually find the way down.
sentences.zh: 你撞到一块岩石，又撞到另一块岩石，再撞到另一块岩石，最后找到下行的路。

sentences.en: So you don't need the skills to do the kind of things that you needed high level skills to do when I started.
sentences.zh: 所以你不再需要我刚开始时所需要的高水平技能，就能做那些事情了。

sentences.en: So there is that element that we've got to be careful of.
sentences.zh: 因此，确实存在我们需要小心的这一因素。

sentences.en: But otherwise, I think it's a really good thing because more people are doing it, more people are interested in seeing these things.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外，我认为这是一件非常好的事情，因为越来越多的人在参与，越来越多的人有兴趣观看这些。

sentences.en: And therefore, that encourages more people to get involved and hopefully at a level that they can manage and hopefully they develop
sentences.zh: 因此，这鼓励了更多的人参与进来，希望是在他们能够应付的水平上，并且希望他们能够发展

sentences.en: and get the skills and maybe go on courses to ensure that they understand the dangers, the challenges, all those sort of things of participating in these sports as well.
sentences.zh: 并获得技能，也许去参加课程，以确保他们了解参与这些运动的危险、挑战以及所有这些方面。

sentences.en: So given the increased interest, do you think that adventure psychology is its own specialty, that it should be recognized as its own specialty or is it just a part of sports
sentences.zh: 鉴于人们兴趣的增加，你认为探险心理学是一个独立的专业吗？它应该被认为是一个独立的专业，还是只是运动心理学的一部分

sentences.en: psychology?
sentences.zh: 心理学？

sentences.en: Yes, that is a really good question.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个非常好的问题。

sentences.en: And my feeling is that the difference between sports psychology and adventure psychology is as broad as the difference between sport and clinical and
sentences.zh: 我的感觉是，运动心理学和探险心理学之间的区别，就像运动与临床、

sentences.en: sport and education and sport and organization or clinical and education and clinical.
sentences.zh: 运动与教育、运动与组织，或者临床与教育、临床之间的区别一样广泛。

sentences.en: And these are very different notions.
sentences.zh: 这些是非常不同的概念。

sentences.en: They're very different notions for a number of reasons.
sentences.zh: 由于多种原因，它们是非常不同的概念。

sentences.en: One is that the idea of what an effective outcome is very different.
sentences.zh: 首先，什么是有成效的结果，其观念非常不同。

sentences.en: In a sport context, it's about winning and it's about doing that sort of things.
sentences.zh: 在体育语境中，这是关于获胜，是关于做那种事情。

sentences.en: That has been translated, let's say, into mountaineering in the terms of conquering EvereSt. No extreme athletes would consider they're conquering EvereSt.
sentences.zh: 比方说，这已经转化为登山领域的“征服珠穆朗玛峰”。没有任何极限运动员会认为他们在征服珠穆朗玛峰。

sentences.en: They know full well that Everest doesn't even know that they're on the mountain, let alone that it's a competition.
sentences.zh: 他们心里很清楚，珠穆朗玛峰甚至不知道他们在山上，更不用说这是一场比赛了。

sentences.en: They also know that if Everest did know that, that they'd snuff them out in a second with the weather conditions.
sentences.zh: 他们也知道，如果珠穆朗玛峰真的知道了，单凭天气条件它就会在一秒钟内让他们灰飞烟灭。

sentences.en: The other element, of course, is getting to the top of Everest is not the goal.
sentences.zh: 当然，另一个因素是，登上珠穆朗玛峰并不是终极目标。

sentences.en: Getting back down again safely is the goal.
sentences.zh: 安全返回才是目标。

sentences.en: Whereas in a sport context, getting to the top would be considered the goal.
sentences.zh: 而在体育语境中，到达顶峰将被视为目标。

sentences.en: So, that's one thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一回事。

sentences.en: The second element that's really important, as I said earlier on, is the fact that you're participating in environments that are not constrained
sentences.zh: 正如我刚才所说，第二个非常重要的要素是，你所参与的环境并不受白线限制，

sentences.en: by white lines, you know, that's in, that's out, and all those kinds of things.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这是界内，那是界外，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So, there are elements within the environment that you actually have to determine, decide what, what is an appropriate way to move this environment.
sentences.zh: 因此，环境中的一些因素需要你亲自去判断，决定在这个环境中行进的合适方式是什么。

sentences.en: There aren't lines that say, no, no, you can't go there because now it's out.
sentences.zh: 没有划好的线告诉你，不，不，你不能去那里，因为现在出界了。

sentences.en: And then, of course, the most serious element, and there's a few other things as well,
sentences.zh: 然后，当然是最严重的因素——虽然还有其他一些事情——

sentences.en: but the most serious element is if things do go wrong, it's not a matter of, oh, well, I've lost the game, never mind, we'll train a bit harder next time, you're dead.
sentences.zh: 但最严重的因素是，如果事情真的出了问题，可不是“哦，好吧，我输了这场比赛，没关系，下次我们刻苦训练”那么简单，你会死的。

sentences.en: There isn't a sort of an opportunity to say, okay, well, I'll come back alive and I'll train a bit harder next time and I'll give it a go next time.
sentences.zh: 没有那种机会说：“好吧，我活着回来，下次我刻苦训练，下次我再试试。”

sentences.en: You're dead.
sentences.zh: 你会死。

sentences.en: You don't have that capacity.
sentences.zh: 你没有那种能力。

sentences.en: So, there are very different activities, even though they involve physical activity, even though there's an element of having to organize, plan, train.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些是非常不同的活动，尽管它们涉及体育活动，尽管其中包含组织、计划和训练的元素。

sentences.en: In the end, I would say that sport and adventure are as different as sport and clinical.
sentences.zh: 最后，我想说运动和探险的区别，就像运动和临床医学的区别一样大。

sentences.en: So, do you think that people who don't necessarily engage in adventure sports, but do other things, for example, controlled adventures, ziplining or some of these outdoor
sentences.zh: 那么，你认为那些不一定从事探险运动，但做其他事情的人，例如受控探险、滑索或其中一些户外绳网课程，能否获得与真正探险运动者所获得的相同的益处？

sentences.en: ropes courses, can they derive some of the same benefits that an actual adventure sports person achieves?
sentences.zh: 我确实这么认为。
